# Leicestershire logistics firm unveils major expansion after nearly 32% growth

28 Aug 2026 | by MHW Magazine Team | Logistics, News

Translink plans to turn its 66,000 sq ft Narborough site into a major indoor pallet sortation centre

A fast-growing Leicestershire logistics firm has announced a major leadership shake-up and plans for a huge new pallet sortation centre after recording almost 32% growth in two years.

Translink Express Logistics has made four senior appointments as the family-run business prepares to celebrate its 40th anniversary next summer.

Three existing employees have been promoted, with Lee Barrett becoming head of traffic, Dan Green taking on the newly created role of head of project management, and Shanice Walsh appointed head of operations.

Ryan Wallis has also joined the company as head of warehousing.

The new management team will take greater responsibility for the day-to-day running of the business, allowing its directors to focus more closely on longer-term growth plans.

# Distributor scales to £35m with a team of 18

Posted on Tuesday 1 September 2026 Share: 

ET Browne UK, the business behind the Palmer’s skincare brand, has built a £35m-plus UK and European operation run by 18 people by outsourcing warehousing and distribution to Europa Worldwide Group for almost 20 years.

THE DARTFORD operation handles between five and ten consignments every day, from single-pallet shipments to full trailer loads, feeding more than 100 retail distribution centres and wholesalers in the UK alongside customers across Poland, the Netherlands, Germany and other European markets.

Palmer’s is stocked by Boots, Tesco, Superdrug and Sainsbury’s. With more than 100 products imported from the United States, the operation must absorb delayed containers and changing import schedules while still hitting strict retail delivery windows.

# Hawks Haulage joins Palletways UK network

Leicester-based logistics provider, Hawks Haulage, has joined the Palletways UK network, marking a key milestone in its strategic growth plans.

Founded in 2019 by Pardeep Virk as a single-truck operation, the company has rapidly grown into a thriving, family-run logistics outfit, now operating a fleet of 35 vehicles and employing 40 staff.

The decision to join Palletways – Europe’s largest express palletised freight network – represents a strategic move to further enhance the business’ offering to customers, while maintaining the personalised service that has underpinned Hawks Haulage’s success.

It comes amid major growth plans which also include further fleet expansions, technological upgrades, staff development and investment in a new state-of-the-art warehouse facility capable of storing up to 2,500 pallets.

This development is set to strengthen the firm’s operational infrastructure, enabling greater efficiency, improving storage solutions and supporting future expansion into integrated logistics services.

August 14, 2026

XDP expands Carlisle capacity for irregular and out-of-gauge freight flows. The 4,941ft² depot serves 67 northern and Scottish postcodes. 

#### IN Brief:

- XDP's new Carlisle depot provides 4,941ft² of operational space.
- The facility serves 67 postcodes across north-west England and southern Scotland.
- XDP says the site adds regional capacity and supports shorter transit times across the coverage area.

XDP has opened a 4,941ft² depot in Carlisle to increase regional capacity for irregular and out-of-gauge freight across north-west England and southern Scotland.

The facility is fully operational and serves 67 postcodes. XDP says the location closes a gap in its regional network and is intended to support shorter transit times and additional capacity for customers across the surrounding area.

# Palletways sees 13.5% profit rise in year before sale to Waterland

By Carol Millett 2026-08-24T16:22:00+01:00

Palletways UK boosted both profit and turnover in the year before it was purchased by Dutch private equity firm Waterland, its latest annual results have revealed.

Turnover increased 10% to £270.7m in the year to 31 December 2025, while pre-tax profit rose 13.5% to £25.1m.

In its strategic report to the results, the company said it remains focused on developing its membership network and providing distribution services across the UK and Europe.

It added that it was well positioned to continue developing its membership and maintaining service levels in a competitive market.

The strategic report also revealed that Palletways is planning to relocate its national headquarters and core operations to a new 640,000sq ft facility at Fradley Park in Lichfield, Staffordshire.

The site is being developed in partnership with Prologis UK and is intended to consolidate Palletways’ operations and provide additional capacity for future growth.

The award was one of ten presented at a glittering ceremony at the annual awards ceremony organised by leading palletised freight distributor Palletline, held at the International Conference Centre in Edinburgh at which guests were entertained by comedians Conor Burns and Fred MacAuley. The company fended off stiff competition from transport companies across the UK to win the award for Commercial Brilliance, sponsored by Allports.
